title_ar: فضيلة الشيخ الددو يشارك في فعاليات ملتقى الإصلاح الثاني بدولة الكويت
title_en: Sheikh al-Dedew Takes Part in the Proceedings of the Second Islah Forum in the State of Kuwait
body_ar: يشارك فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء ورئيس جمعية المستقبل للدعوة والثقافة والتعليم ورئيس جامعة عبد الله بن ياسين في ملتقى الإصلاح الثاني الذي تنظمه جمعية الإصلاح الاجتماعي بدولة الكويت تحت شعار: "هل نحن قوم عمليون ؟" ويستمر الملتقى ثلاثة أيام ابتداء من أمس السبت 22 جمادى الأولى 1443هـ الموافق: 14 إبريل 2012 ولغاية غد الاثنين، ويتضمن برنامج الملتقى محاضرات سيلقيها فضيلة الشيخ أمام المشاركين في الملتقى وعلى هامش الملتقى الذي سيجمع أرباب الدعوة والفكر من مختلف أقطار العالم دكاترة علميين ومشايخ ربانيين. وقد ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو أمس السبت محاضرة هامة تحت عنوان: سنن التغيير، وتتكون المحاضرة حسبما جاء في موقع المتلقى على الشبكة من ثلاثة محاور هي: توضيح أهمية التغيير داخل المؤسسات الدعوية للوصول إلى أعلى درجات الفاعلية، وسرد أمثلة من التاريخ الإسلامي للتغيير الناجح في القيادات والمنهجيات، والتأصيل الشرعي حول التمسك بالمناصب في حال إعاقة القيادة التقدم في العمل الدعوي، وسنقوم برفع المحاضرة قريبا على الموقع إن شاء الله. وبعد اختتام الملتقى سيشارك فضيلة الشيخ بحر الأسبوع الجاري في ملتقى العطاء الثالث، والذي تحتضنه مدينة أبها بالمملكة العربية السعودية.
body_en:
Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew — president of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, president of the Future Association for Calling to Islam, Culture and Education, and president of Abdullah ibn Yasin University — is taking part in the Second Islah Forum, organised by the Social Reform Society in the State of Kuwait under the banner "Are We a Practical People?" The forum runs for three days, beginning yesterday, Saturday 22 Jumada al-Ula 1443 AH, corresponding to 14 April 2012, and continuing until tomorrow, Monday. The forum's programme takes in lectures which the Sheikh will deliver before the forum's participants and on its margins; the forum will bring together the leading figures of the call to Islam (daʿwah) and of thought from the various regions of the world — academic doctors and God-fearing sheikhs.

Yesterday, Saturday, Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew delivered an important lecture under the title "God's Established Ways in Change". According to what appeared on the forum's website, the lecture consists of three axes: setting out the importance of change within the institutions of the call so as to reach the highest degrees of effectiveness; the recounting of examples from Islamic history of successful change in leaderships and in methods; and the grounding in the Sharia of the matter of clinging to office where the leadership obstructs progress in the work of the call. We shall upload the lecture to the site shortly, God willing.

After the forum's conclusion the Sheikh will take part, in the course of the present week, in the Third Giving Forum, hosted by the city of Abha in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.

options: preserve 1443 as served and record the conflict
read 1433, which is what 14 April 2012 corresponds to
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT. 22 Jumada al-Ula 1443 AH falls in December 2021, not April 2012; the intended year is plainly 1433. The Arabic is preserved as served and the English carries the error rather than repairing it, per style guide section 11. Flagged so the Arabic can be corrected centrally.

flags.arabic: التأصيل الشرعي حول التمسك بالمناصب في حال إعاقة القيادة التقدم في العمل الدعوي
flags.context: the third axis of the lecture, as the forum's website described it
options: render as the source has it, with the ruling not stated
infer the ruling from the framing
flags.note: Style guide section 10. The third axis announces a grounding in the Sharia of the question whether a leader may hold on to office when his leadership is obstructing the work — a pointed question, and one whose answer the record does not give. The framing leans one way; the English must not. 'التأصيل الشرعي' is rendered 'the grounding in the Sharia' with no ruling word attached. Note also that this description is the forum website's, at a third remove from the Sheikh: the news desk is quoting another site's programme note.

HOMONYM WARNING, the same one as records 783 and 786. The glossary's سنن ('the sunnah acts', worship) must not be applied: sunan here are the constant patterns God has set governing how change occurs in human societies. Rendered 'God's established ways' for consistency across this slice; 'The Laws of Change' reads better in English but imports a determinism the Arabic does not carry.

flags.context: وبعد اختتام الملتقى سيشارك فضيلة الشيخ بحر الأسبوع الجاري
options: in the course of the present week
at the end of the present week
flags.note: في بحر الأسبوع is an Arabic journalistic idiom for 'in the course of' a period, not 'at the sea of'. It is idiom rather than dialect, but it is opaque to a reader working from the dictionary, and it is recorded here because it recurs in this news section.

flags.context: تتكون المحاضرة حسبما جاء في موقع المتلقى على الشبكة
options: read as الملتقى, 'the forum', as the record spells it five other times
flags.note: The same transposition as in record 788 (المتلقى for الملتقى), which suggests a habit of the news desk rather than a one-off. Preserved and flagged.

translator_notes: A news-desk announcement written while the forum was still running; the last paragraph is forward-looking and the site's undertaking to upload the lecture may or may not have been kept.
The CMS timestamp, 15 April 2012, is a bulk-upload date.

'جمعية الإصلاح الاجتماعي' is the Social Reform Society, a long-established Kuwaiti body; its name is translated rather than transliterated, while the forum it runs is left as the 'Islah Forum' because that is how it is known in English-language coverage. A reviewer may prefer to harmonise the two.
'مشايخ ربانيين' is rendered 'God-fearing sheikhs'; rabbānī carries the sense of a scholar whose learning is joined to devotion, and no single English word holds both.
